name: Inflow
one_liner: ADHD app for adults: short daily CBT-based lessons and exercises on focus, procrastination and emotions, plus community and optional coaching.
best_for: Adults with ADHD, diagnosed or suspected, who want to learn CBT-based coping skills
People on ADHD medication who want skills training alongside it
Adults who want short daily lessons on focus, planning and procrastination
People who would like group or coach support as part of a program
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
Children and teens (it is made for adults)
People who need an ADHD diagnosis or medication (Inflow does not diagnose or prescribe)
People who want a free app: the full program needs a subscription after the trial
short_description: A subscription app for adults with ADHD with daily CBT-based modules, exercises, a peer community and optional coaching. Owned by Cerebral since March 2026.
long_description: Inflow is an app for adults with ADHD built on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) principles. Each day you work through short modules and exercises on topics such as focus, procrastination, time management and emotions, and you can join a community of other adults with ADHD; higher plans add coaching. It does not diagnose ADHD or prescribe medication. After a 7-day free trial, Inflow's FAQ lists $199/year or $47.99/month; cheaper plans without coaching have been reported in the App Store, so check the price in the app. Two studies of the app have been published, both with authors tied to the company: a 2022 open study of 240 adults found it usable and most 7-week users reported fewer symptoms, and a 2025 randomized trial of 154 adults found greater improvement in inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms and quality of life than a waitlist, but not in daily functioning. Its privacy policy says it uses cookies and tracking for targeted advertising (you can opt out in the app). Cerebral, an online mental health company, bought Inflow in March 2026; the two run as separate platforms for now.
patient_summary: You do short daily lessons and exercises based on CBT for adult ADHD, and can join a community or, on higher plans, get coaching. It starts with a 7-day free trial, then costs $199/year or $47.99/month on the plan listed in Inflow's FAQ. It does not diagnose or prescribe, so pair it with a clinician if you need those.

pricing.notes: 7-day free trial. Inflow's FAQ lists $199/year or $47.99/month; reviews report App Store plans without coaching at about $95.99/year or $22.49/month. Inflow mentions an affordability program and a student discount. Some users report unexpected annual renewals, so note your renewal date.

privacy.notes: Says it does not sell personal information for money or use sensitive data for cross-context ads, but uses cookies and tracking for targeted advertising (opt-out in the app's privacy settings). Owner Cerebral faced a 2024 FTC order over sharing health data with advertisers, before it bought Inflow.

seo.title: Inflow: ADHD Management App for Adults | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: Inflow is an ADHD app for adults with CBT-based skill building, focus tools, and community support. From $9.99/month. Developed with ADHD specialists.

faqs.a: Inflow is a comprehensive ADHD management app for adults featuring CBT-based learning modules, focus tools, habit tracking, and an active peer support community.
Inflow offers a free tier with limited access. Premium is $9.99/month (annual billing) or $14.99/month. A 7-day free trial is available. FSA/HSA eligible.
No, Inflow is not FDA cleared. It is a wellness app designed to complement ADHD medication and therapy, not replace clinical treatment.

faqs.q: What skills does Inflow teach for ADHD?
faqs.a: Inflow's CBT-based curriculum covers focus, procrastination, emotional regulation, time management, organization, and sleep - all adapted specifically for adults with ADHD.

primary_uses: Daily CBT-based lessons for adult ADHD
Exercises for focus, planning and procrastination
Peer community of adults with ADHD

clinical_trials.study: 8 weeks of Inflow vs waitlist in adults with ADHD

citation.title: Bridging the Gap: Digital CBT for Adults Managing ADHD Challenges

clinical_trials.outcome: App group improved more than waitlist on inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms and ADHD quality of life, not on functional impairment. Lead author reports ties to Inflow.

clinical_trials.study: 7-week open usability and feasibility study of Inflow

citation.authors: Knouse LE, Hu X, Sachs G, Isaacs S
citation.title: Usability and feasibility of a cognitive-behavioral mobile app for ADHD in adults

clinical_trials.outcome: Usability rated favorably; most 7-week users self-reported fewer ADHD symptoms and less impairment. No control group; two authors are Inflow co-founders.

availability.note: Acquired by Cerebral in March 2026; still offered as its own app on iPhone and Android.
